key_insight: Resolving the electric field around growing bubbles shows that current density, Ohmic losses, and bubble motion are strongly geometry-dependent, especially on patterned micro-electrode arrays.
engineering_relevance: Electrode patterning and bubble spacing can be designed to delay electrode blockage and reduce resistive losses in water electrolysis.
method: 3D VOF simulations with phase change in Basilisk
Primary electric field solved to obtain non-uniform current density and gas production
Single-bubble and multi-bubble growth studied on electrodes and catalytic island arrays
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based comparison of single-bubble and multi-bubble cases, with footprint tracking and theory used to explain outward drift and its 1/d2 scaling.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on idealized simulated geometries and electrochemical field coupling, so experimental validation will be needed before direct design transfer.
paper_title: Bubble growth on arrays of micro-electrodes
